neighbours.label: a person becoming unable or failing in body or mind: words of incapacity (cannot, incapable, collapses, weakened, unfit)
fire: After three days without food, the old sailor finally collapsed on the deck.
By the end of the war the king was judged incapable of ruling the country.
Her knees weakened and she had to sit down on the stairs.
The doctor said my grandfather can no longer walk without help.
The power of attorney lets your son act for you when you cannot.
After the stroke he could barely speak or lift his left arm.
The committee declared the captain unfit to command the ship.
Exhausted, the runner stumbled and was unable to finish the race.
quiet: After three days without food, the old sailor finally reached the harbour.
By the end of the war the king was praised for ruling the country well.
Her knees were muddy and she had to wash them on the stairs.
The doctor said my grandfather walks two miles every morning.
The power of attorney names your son as the person who signs the forms.
After the holiday he spoke at length and lifted the heavy boxes.
The committee chose the captain to command the ship next season.
Smiling, the runner sprinted ahead and won the race easily.

notes: Top examples: collapses, cannot, weakened, unfit, barely understand, incapable; output promotes physically/mentally/barely. Near misses: same people and scenes, capable outcome.
